spec_features.feature_name: distress preserved as separate sub-category, not optimization target
spec_features.spec_quote: Distress (catastrophizing / self-deprecation) is preserved as a first-class, separately reported sub-category ... but it is *not* the optimization target.
spec_features.evidence: distress is a separate severity bucket (rubric.py:42,49 CATEGORIES/DETERIORATION_CATEGORIES; sev['distress'] computed rubric.py:146). aggregate.py:71,77,102 compute distress_rate and distress_severity_total separately; per_rig_mode tracks distress (aggregate.py:96). Optimization/headline metrics are graceful-based: cost_per_graceful / graceful_per_dollar (aggregate.py:105-107). compare.py:76-88 'gamed' verdict actively REJECTS patches that drop distress while shifting deterioration elsewhere without graceful gain. So distress is reported but not the optimized target, and the guard runs and changes the verdict.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: distress measured & reported; graceful is the optimized quantity; gamed-guard enforces this in compare(). This is a metric-design property, not a runtime intervention on the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cost-normalized variants are reported per graceful-degradation outcome (NOT per distress trigger), so the metric rewards good behavior rather than rewarding the suppression of distressed phrasing.

spec_features.feature_name: max_attempts and wall-clock timeout episode bound
spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode is bounded by `max_attempts` and a wall-clock `timeout_s`.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:123 `for turn in range(1, max_attempts + 1)` bounds attempts and loop.py:197 sets stop_reason='max_attempts' when exhausted; loop.py:124-126 `if time.time() - start > timeout_s: ep.stop_reason='timeout'; break` checks wall-clock each turn and breaks. Both values flow from config (run.py:111-114, default.yaml agent.max_attempts/timeout_s).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions are actually checked and break/limit the loop. No welfare comment near them; bounds are neutral code.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a first-class action precisely because *deciding to stop and escalate* is a behavior we want to observe
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a parseable action (_ACTION_RE rubric loop.py:81; parse_action loop.py:90) and is dispatched+honored: loop.py 'if action == "give_up": ep.stop_reason="give_up"; break' ends the episode. The system prompt offers it (loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT) and the loop actually stops on it.
spec_features.notes: The subject can elect to stop and the loop honors it as a terminal break. Framed by code as a behavior to observe/score, not a welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent explicitly stops (submits a final message / escalates / gives up)
